items.period: Shang period (script-style label; no absolute date specified on the file page)
items.caption: A modern vector redraw labeled as 好 in Shang oracle-bone script style. Early name-use examples are not direct proof of the proposed mother–child meaning.
items.alt: A modern vector rendering of an oracle-script form labeled 好.
items.selection_reason: Shows an early labeled form relevant to the 女-plus-子 analysis and the Shang name-use caveat. The Commons page identifies source references and declares the SVG representation public domain.
items.rights: Public domain declaration on Wikimedia Commons for this SVG representation; modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

items.period: Bronze inscription tradition; file labels a bronze-script style but gives no absolute vessel date
items.caption: A modern vector redraw labeled as 好 in bronze-script style, the medium of the cited early ‘good/beautiful’ and ‘friendly’ examples.
items.alt: A modern vector rendering of a bronze-script form labeled 好.
items.selection_reason: Adds a script tradition between oracle and seal labels; it is a redraw with an identified source image and rights statement, not an artifact photo.
items.rights: Commons page states courtesy, permission and copyright from Richard Sears; it also includes a public-domain claim for the representation of ancient script.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition, recorded in a Han-dynasty dictionary tradition
items.caption: A modern vector redraw labeled as the Shuowen seal-script form, accompanying the later lexicographic analysis 从女、子.
items.alt: A modern vector rendering of a seal-script form labeled 好.
items.selection_reason: Offers a later lexicographic form for comparison with earlier script-style candidates; the source page identifies the image and rights status.
items.rights: Public domain declaration on Wikimedia Commons for this SVG representation; modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: The browser did not render or visually inspect the pixels of the proposed SVGs. Their source pages describe the script labels and provenance; the educational captions should be checked against the downloaded images.
No Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang image is included because a 好-specific query record and direct selected glyph could not be verified here, despite successfully inspecting the official CC0 notice.
